name: Azariah
overview: Azariah was a male Levite from the tribe of Levi, specifically a Merarite, who lived during the reign of King Hezekiah. He is uniquely identified as the son of Jehallelel, serving in a priestly capacity among the Merarites, descendants of Merari, a son of Levi. His role is noted in the context of temple service and Levitical duties.
namesAndTitles: The name Azariah means 'YHWH has helped,' reflecting a divine assistance theme common in Hebrew names. This proper name, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 29:12, was not given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotation consistent with his Levitical heritage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Azariah as the son of Jehallelel, establishing his family lineage within the Merarite clan of the Levites. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the provided references.
scriptureSignificance: Azariah's significance lies in his Levitical role during King Hezekiah's reign, a period marked by temple restoration and religious reform. As a Merarite, he was part of the priestly tribe tasked with sacred duties, underscoring the importance of faithful service to God. His lineage and service highlight the continuity of Levitical responsibilities amid Judah's spiritual renewal.
